question.text:
If $\cos \theta+i \sin \theta, \theta \in \mathbb{R}$, is the root of the equation
$a_0 x^n+a_1 \cdot x^{n-1}+\ldots .+a_{n-1} x+a_n=0, a_0, a_1, \ldots \ldots . a_n \in \mathbb{R}, a_0 \neq 0$
then the value of $a_1 \sin \theta+a_2 \sin 2 \theta+\ldots .+a_n \sin n \theta$ is

solution.text:
Hint: $a_0 x^n+a_1 \cdot x^{n-1}+\ldots .+a_{n-1} x+a_n=0$
divided by $x^n$
$a_0+a_1 \frac{1}{x}+\ldots \ldots+a_{n-1} \frac{1}{x^{n-1}}+a_n \frac{1}{x^n}=0$
put $x=\cos \theta+i \sin \theta$ and equating imaginary part
$a_1 \sin \theta+a_2 \sin 2 \theta+\ldots .+a_n \sin 2 \theta=0$
